# Introduction

This report totals retail sales by calendar quarter from `data/retail_sales.xlsx`. It shows the totals as a table and as a bar chart with a line over the same values.

# Setup

```{r}
#| label: load-packages
library(readxl)
library(dplyr)
library(lubridate)
library(gt)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)
```

```{r}
#| label: load-data
sales <- read_excel("data/retail_sales.xlsx")
```

The data has `{r} format(nrow(sales), big.mark = ",")` rows.

# Quarterly totals

`order_date` is converted to a `Date`. Sales are then summed by calendar quarter, with the year included so that the same quarter in different years stays separate.

```{r}
#| label: aggregate-quarterly
quarterly <- sales |>
       mutate(
              order_date = as.Date(order_date),
              quarter = floor_date(order_date, "quarter")
       ) |>
       summarise(total_sales = sum(sales, na.rm = TRUE), .by = quarter) |>
       arrange(quarter) |>
       mutate(label = paste0(year(quarter), " Q", quarter(quarter)))
```

The data covers `{r} nrow(quarterly)` quarters, from `{r} quarterly$label[1]` to `{r} quarterly$label[nrow(quarterly)]`.

```{r}
#| label: quarterly-table
quarterly |>
  select(label, total_sales) |>
  gt() |>
  cols_label(label = "Quarter", total_sales = "Total sales") |>
  fmt_currency(total_sales, decimals = 0) |>
  tab_header(title = "Quarterly retail sales")
```

# Quarterly sales chart

```{r}
#| label: quarterly-plot
ggplot(quarterly, aes(x = label, y = total_sales, group = 1)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_dollar()) +
  labs(x = "Quarter", y = "Total sales", title = "Quarterly retail sales") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

In the chart, Q4 is the highest quarter in each year and Q1 is the lowest or close to it. Sales are higher overall in 2018 than in 2015.

# Notes

- Some order IDs appear on more than one row. These look like separate line items, so all rows are summed as they are. The data was not checked for exact duplicate rows.
